proposals.evidence: CDIAL 13845 *sphuṭyati explicitly records Shina phuṭoiki break. Degener cites this entry for transitive phuṭ- and separately records intransitive phuṭ- break/be broken, with present phuṭin and past phuṭili. The present proposal concerns that intransitive lemma. Its identical stem and explicit paradigm support the same historical family, but the transitivity difference from Turner’s Shina gloss is retained; no direction of a zero-marked transitivity derivation is asserted.

proposals.detailedEvidence: CDIAL 10452 tentatively derives the Shina walking verb (Gilgiti yay-, Kohistani yaz-, Guresi yāž-) from the future yāsyati through *yāssa/*yāsa. The isolated Kharmang and Drasi imperative yās is compared with that sibilant-stem series; the final s is preserved. Turner marks the Shina derivation possible, and Degener likewise prints T. 10452 with a question mark, so this is a difficult proposal rather than a secure regular present-stem reflex. Schmidt Astori yazō̌nu to walk is grouped with this same tentative series: Turner explicitly cites Kohistani yazōnu. Its medial z makes the family comparison closer than the imperative alone, but does not remove the uncertainty of the future-stem derivation. Schmidt Kohistani yāzō̌n to walk preserves the explicitly cited z-bearing stem, with initial vowel length and absence of final u retained as source variation. Schmidt Gurezi yajō̌nu to walk supplies the corresponding voiced affricate notation alongside Turner’s Gurezi yāžōnu; this comparison does not strengthen the tentative future-stem reconstruction.
